newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA's unit says new machines to boost '97.
newsitem.headline: SCA's unit says new machines to boost '97.

text.p: New production technology at Swedish Molnlycke's nappy factory in Falkenberg will halve production costs, the unit of Sweden's forestry company SCA said on Tuesday.

The machines were put into use last autumn and during 1997 will have a positive effect of up to 50 million crowns on Molnlycke's result, company managing director Kurth Augustson told a breakfast meeting in Gothenburg.
"This will take effect fully in 1997 and will give an effect of less than 50 million crowns," Augustson said.
The factory in Falkenberg accounts for about a third of Molnlycke's nappy production.
Molnlycke's nappy strategy is to focus on its private brand label which Augustson estimates can grow from the current level of 15 to 20 percent of the total nappy market.
Private labels are retailers' brands, which retailers market themselves so producers do not have to foot advertising bills as with their own brands, making prices lower, he said.
Molnlycke aims to increase its share of the private label market share in Europe to 50 percent from the current level of about 25 percent.
Augustson said the competition on this segment was not so tough in Europe.
However nappies were starting to have less importance for Molnlycke as a whole.
The biggest and quickest growth area for Molnylucke is incontinent products.

These products account for 38 percent of Molnlycke's sales and Molnlycke is biggest in the world in this area with room for further growth in both Europe and North America through acquisitions, Augustson said.
